definitions.explanation: The traditional craft of sewing Japanese clothing such as kimono, yukata, and other traditional garments. Uses techniques distinct from Western dressmaking.

examples.japanese: {和裁|わさい}を{習|なら}っている。
{祖母|そぼ}は{和裁|わさい}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: My grandmother has Japanese sewing skills.

examples.japanese: {和裁|わさい}の{職人|しょくにん}は{年々|ねんねん}{減少|げんしょう}しており、{技術|ぎじゅつ}の{継承|けいしょう}が{課題|かだい}となっている。
examples.english: The number of Japanese sewing artisans is declining year by year, and passing on the techniques has become a challenge.

notes:
A compound of {和|わ} (Japanese) and {裁|さい} (cutting/sewing). Contrasted with {洋裁|ようさい} (Western-style dressmaking). Japanese sewing uses different techniques — kimono are sewn entirely by hand with straight seams, and the fabric can be taken apart and resewn.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和裁|わさい}を{習|なら}う: to learn Japanese sewing
- {和裁|わさい}{教室|きょうしつ}: Japanese sewing class
- {和裁|わさい}{士|し}: certified Japanese sewing professional
- {和裁|わさい}の{技術|ぎじゅつ}: Japanese sewing techniques

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {洋裁|ようさい}: Western-style dressmaking — cutting and sewing Western clothing
- {裁縫|さいほう}: sewing — general term for all sewing
- {仕立|した}て: tailoring — making garments to order
